book.title: Happy-Go-Lucky
book.summary: David Sedaris, the “champion storyteller,” (Los Angeles Times) returns with his first new collection of personal essays since the bestselling Calypso Back when restaurant menus were still printed on paper, and wearing a mask—or not—was a decision made mostly on Halloween, David Sedaris spent his time doing normal things. As Happy-Go-Lucky opens, he is learning to shoot guns with his sister, visiting muddy flea markets in Serbia, buying gummy worms to feed to ants, and telling his nonagenarian father wheelchair jokes. But then the pandemic hits, and like so many others, he’s stuck in lockdown, unable to tour and read for audiences, the part of his work he loves most. To cope, he walks for miles through a nearly deserted city, smelling only his own breath.

argument.statement: The pandemic disrupts ordinary life and Sedaris’s touring work, leaving him to cope with isolation through solitary walks and personal observation.

book.rationale: The book is primarily a collection of personal essays reflecting Sedaris's own experiences and thoughts, making it a strong fit for Memoir & Autobiography, with societal reflections that warrant inclusion of Society & Culture as a secondary subject.
